reference.name: K1_D96_ROW_STRIPED
reference.binary_event_operation: select signed INT8 weight then accumulate

fc1_handoff_spot_check.qualification: This verifies the handoff population and identity only; it is not an FC1 cycle or speedup result.

primary_sparse_reference.reason: Every selected patch activation is exact binary, so the K1 sparse baseline also eliminates activation multiplication. Pricing 96 MACs only on K1 would charge it for work not required by either sparse design.

dense_mac_reference.reason: A 96-INT8-MAC accelerator remains useful as a conventional dense context baseline, but is not the matched sparse baseline.

patch_advance_gate.reason: The best legal point is 1.104921x and the M218-like legal point is 0.946285x. The only listed point above 1.5x needs sixteen 128-bit bank equivalents and 256 lanes.

contribution_ruling.m216_m218_role_after_m223: supporting context/request-update amortization candidate, not a strong general performance contribution
contribution_ruling.fc1_as_third_contribution: candidate only after M224 strong-baseline evidence
contribution_ruling.paper_target: two or three non-overlapping mechanisms; baselines, miters, negative screens, and superseded milestones remain supporting evidence

findings.title: M221 still exposes the superseded M216/M218 performance-contribution map
findings.evidence: M221 calls C3 the strongest current new architectural contribution and a strong standalone FC2 result, while M223 correctly marks M216/M218_as_primary_performance_contribution=false. M223 does not explicitly supersede the M221 contribution-map entry in its supersedes list.
findings.required_action: Before paper or unified handoff, issue a successor master contribution/replacement ledger that cites M223 and marks the M221 C3 performance wording superseded. Do not edit sealed M221 evidence.

findings.title: The logical K1/D96 reference still lacks an equal-capacity physical SRAM/routing realization
findings.evidence: The add-only operation is the right fair baseline, but fixed six-of-eight row striping can imbalance depth; equal-capacity rotation adds selection and lane permutation. M223 retains the M222 ideal cycle screen and correctly claims no RTL/DC, so the negative screen is valid but not a physical comparison.
findings.required_action: Carry the row-placement, bank-depth, selector/routing, accumulator-port, and commit-interface caveats into any future matched RTL or paper comparison.

findings.title: The FC1 pivot population is not identity-bound inside M223
findings.evidence: Independent inspection found 100/100 selected bitpacks matching the verified M51 manifest across ten FC1 modules, but M223 names only counts and stages and does not bind the manifest SHA, selected module indices, or per-file hashes.
findings.required_action: M224 must bind manifest SHA 2a5e6e..., enumerate module indices 6/8/11/13/16/18/20/22/24/26, verify all 100 bitpacks, and keep the stage-3 conventional exclusion explicit.

findings.title: Acc19 is a handoff assertion rather than a bound proof in M223
findings.evidence: M223 states accumulator_width=19 but neither derives the bound nor cites a sealed width-proof artifact. No FC1 result is admitted, so this is not a current correctness failure.
findings.required_action: M224 should bind or reproduce the signed range proof, including bias/residual/quantization assumptions.

findings.title: The two stage-3 nonbinary FC1 identities are policy-only in M223
findings.evidence: The conventional-path rule is safe, but M223 does not name the two excluded modules or bind the evidence that their activations are nonbinary.
findings.required_action: Record their exact module identities and nonbinary evidence in M224 or the final operator coverage ledger.
